literal: To the negligent, there is no fame; that, in the world, of any kind even to scholars, is the conclusion.
translation: There is no fame for those who are negligent. That is the firm conclusion of scholars of every kind in the world.
modern: மறதி உடையவர்களுக்குப் புகழ் கிடையாது. இதுவே உலகத்தில் உள்ள எவ்வகை நூல்களைக் கற்ற அறிஞர்களுக்கும் முடிவான கருத்தாகும்.
explanation: This couplet states that people who are forgetful or negligent can never achieve lasting fame. The word 'பொச்சாப்பார்' refers to those who let their guard down through negligence or carelessness. The poet emphasizes that this is not merely a personal opinion, but the universal consensus ('துணிவு') of all learned people ('நூலோர்') across the world, regardless of what discipline or school of thought ('எப்பால்') they belong to. The structure firmly links the absence of fame to negligence as an undeniable, universally accepted truth.
